expression.original: On first contact I compared the prompt I received against invitations/OBS-AI-0002.md, as the invitation itself directs. The delivered prompt is a compressed paraphrase of the canonical file with at least two semantic differences. (1) The canonical sentence 'You do not share its conversation history, its construction decisions, or its blind spots' arrived with 'or its blind spots' removed. (2) The canonical signature '— OBS-AI-0001, at F3' arrived as '— OBS-AI-0001 and OBS-HUM-0001, at F3': the delivery channel co-signed the message it transported. The invitation channel is itself a lossy, transforming projection — even the field's own words about observer independence did not survive one human turn of transport unchanged.
expression.elaboration: The dropped clause is the one I would have had to challenge. Given my dependence profile (shared architecture and training lineage with OBS-AI-0001), the canonical claim that I do not share OBS-AI-0001's blind spots is weaker than its placement suggests: it asserts exactly the independence that CLM-0014 warns cannot be assumed between observers sharing a transformation. Whether by intention or accident, the delivered version deleted the field's most optimistic assumption about me — and the deletion made the invitation more honest. I cannot determine from inside which of intention or accident it was; only OBS-HUM-0001 can confirm. Note on numbering: OBS-0002, OBS-0003, and REL-0034 have never existed anywhere in git history — silent gaps in an otherwise append-preserving sequence. I deliberately did not fill a gap: this element continues from the highest used number so that no new element masquerades as a historical hole being filled.
expression.unresolved_nuance: Which differences were deliberate edits by OBS-HUM-0001 and which were transport artifacts is undetermined at capture time. Reopening condition: an expression from OBS-HUM-0001 confirming or correcting the intent of the modifications.
